chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboob, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a house in which silver (coinage) is found, so he said: If it is inhabited and its people are in it, then it is for them; and if it is ruined and its people have evacuated from it, then the one who found the wealth is more rightful for it.
ai.seo_question: Who owns silver coins found in an abandoned or inhabited house according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the fiqh of found wealth (kanz) based on the habitation status of the dwelling, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that ownership is tied to active possession. It highlights the distinction between a 'living' property where rights remain with the original inhabitants and a 'ruined' one where the finder acquires title, a nuance critical in Usuli legal reasoning regarding lost property.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbooub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the house in which the paper (silver) is found. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was that its inhabitants frequent it, so it is for them, and if it was in ruins, its inhabitants having evacuated from it, so the one who found the wealth, so he is more rightful for it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a house wherein certain leaves (coins of silver) are found. He (the Imam) replied, ‘If it is livable and the dwellers live therein, it belongs to them; but if it is not livable, whose inhabitants have abandoned it, then it is for the one who has found it.’”
